Cabo Girão by boat from Funchal, Madeira: six seconds of cliff, and two yellow dots.

The dots are buoys. Look just above the middle of the water, side by side, like two small eyes keeping watch on the beach.

Behind them: a strip of grey pebbles, then terraces with a few flat roofs and stone walls, then rock in red and green all the way up and out of the frame. The camera gave up before the cliff did.

Nobody built those terraces for the view. They got it anyway.

Duas boias, uma praia, e uma montanha por cima.

Both our trips come along here from the marina. The Day Trip stops at Fajã dos Padres for the swim and paddle, the Sunset Trip turns at Cabo Girão as the light goes. Your group only, five at most.

Six seconds is the Reel. The boat gives you a bit longer. Book direct on chifbay.com

items.caption:
Madeira swim stop from above: a floating swimmer, a crooked stone wall and the whole Atlantic trying to get in.

The swimmer is on their back, in red, arms out, right of centre. Not a care in the picture.

The wall is the clever part. It bends at an angle like a folded ruler, and behind it the water turns green and clear. On the other side of the rock, the sea is all white foam and dark blue.

Some good planning went into that wall. Or some very patient waves.

The practical bit: swimming is on our Day Trip only. It leaves Funchal marina at 10:00 or 14:00, takes 2h30 or 3h, and stops at Fajã dos Padres for a swim and paddle. The Sunset Trip has no swimming. Both are private, five guests at most, with food on board.

Bring a towel. We will bring the rest.

Dia de mar, sem pressa.

Send us your dates on chifbay.com and we will see what is free.

Madeira from the mountain side: a person in a red jacket, a stone path and a very big drop on both sides.

They are walking away from us, arms out, one hand on each rope. White woolly hat, black leggings. The path is a thin strip of stone steps along a ridge, and the rock on either side falls away into green and grey.

The sky is doing the most. Orange streaks across dark cloud, right over the peak. The path does not seem to mind.

This one is not from the boat, so no sea here. But the island is just as steep where it meets the water, and we see that side from Funchal marina.

Our Day Trip and our Sunset Trip both follow the coast past Câmara de Lobos towards Cabo Girão, one of the highest sea cliffs in Europe. The Day Trip adds a swim and paddle stop at Fajã dos Padres. Both are private, five guests at most, with food on board.

Pés firmes na terra, ou no mar.

Mountain path or sea cliff, which one would you pick first?

Private boat tour from Funchal, Madeira: one straw hat, one hand on the wheel and a very bright sea.

Someone in a long white shirt is standing at the helm, back to us, hair under a straw hat with a black ribbon. One hand rests on the seat, the other on the steering wheel. The two Karnic seats are in front, so the view is not blocked.

The sea on the left is covered in little flashes of light, as if somebody spilled glitter on it. Above, blue sky and small white clouds, and the grey canopy framing it all like a window.

The practical bit: our Day Trip leaves Funchal marina at 10:00 or 14:00 and takes 2h30 or 3h. The Sunset Trip is 2h or 2h30 and leaves 1h15 before the sun goes down, so the time changes through the year. Bring a hat, like this one. Sunglasses help too. We have the food on board.

Private boat, skipper included, five guests at most.

O chapéu já está escolhido.

Cliff boat tour from Funchal, Madeira: the rock is wearing stripes and the farms are sitting on top.

A tall brown wall of rock runs across the middle of the picture. Look closely and it is ribbed, with darker and redder lines all the way down, like somebody combed it.

At the top, the land turns green and flat enough for terraces and a few small white houses. They sit right at the edge and seem completely relaxed about it.

In front, the sea is deep blue, with a bright patch of sparkle on the left. Above, a lot of small white clouds, all in a hurry to go somewhere else.

This is the coast we follow from Funchal marina, past Câmara de Lobos and on towards Cabo Girão. Our Day Trip goes this way and adds a swim and paddle stop at Fajã dos Padres. The Sunset Trip follows the same coast, without swimming. Both are private, five guests at most, with a skipper and food on board.

A costa vista do mar tem outra altura.

Would you look up at the cliff, or down at the water first?

Private boat tour from Funchal, Madeira: two glasses, one windy deck and a hairstyle nobody planned.

Two guests are standing at the back of the boat, and the wind has taken charge. The one on the left is laughing, sunglasses on, one hand holding her hair down and a glass of something pink in the other. The one facing her wears a grey hoodie, and her long dark hair is blowing sideways.

Behind them there is a thin pole with a small camera on top. That is our Insta360, and it records the whole boat while everyone is busy with their hair.

The sky is bright blue with a few white clouds, and the sea behind is open and a little choppy. The hair lost this one.

The practical bit: our Day Trip and our Sunset Trip both leave from Funchal marina. The boat is private, with a skipper, five guests at most, and nobody else on board. The Insta360 video, photos with a real camera and food on board come with every trip.

Vento no cabelo, copo na mão.

Would a windy day on the water suit your group?

Sunset boat tour from Funchal, Madeira: two people on the bow and the sun doing all the work.

Our boat sits on the left of the picture, white hull, dark canopy. Right at the front, two people are sitting on the bow in white tops, looking out at the sun. Nobody is checking a phone. The sun is a small bright disc near the horizon, with a long gold stripe running down the water towards us.

Behind them the coast curves away, green and brown hills with a few houses along the shore. Above, big clouds lit orange from underneath. The water in front is dark, with gold patches that move around like they cannot decide where to land.

The practical bit: our Sunset Trip is 2h or 2h30 and leaves Funchal marina 1h15 before the sun goes down, so the time changes through the year. It follows the same coast as the Day Trip and turns at Cabo Girão or Ribeira Brava. No swimming on this one. It is private, with a skipper, five guests at most, and food on board.

O sol já vai descendo.

Would you take the bow seat, or stay under the canopy?
